about.note: Each entry links its page and revision. `page` differs from the key when the origin is that of the traditional or radical form (学 -> 學).

々.text: One theory holds that it is simplified from 仝, a variant of 同 (“same (used as iteration mark)”), written in cursive.

七.text: A vertical stroke and a horizontal stroke bisecting each other – original character of 切 (“to cut”).

万.text: Scorpion. The derivative 蠆 refers to the original word.

三.text: Three parallel strokes. Triplication of 一 (“one”).

上.text: Short horizontal above long arc (contrast 下).

下.text: Short horizontal below long arc (contrast 上).

不.text: The calyx of a flower. 不 was composed into a phono-semantic character with the pictograph for mouth (口), to form 否, representing “no” (negation).

与.text: Both components are phonetic. The closest version to the original is 𦥸.

世.text: Variant form of 枼 (the original form of 葉 (“leaf”)) with the tree removed.

両.text: According to Shuowen Jiezi an ideogrammic compound (會意): 一 + 㒳.

並.text: Duplication of 立: two people standing side-by-side.

丨.text: According to Shuowen Jiezi, it is a pictogram of a vertical wooden stick. It appears in the original version of 朕, which originally meant "to mend a boat", and in 尹, in which the stick symbolizes authority.

中.text: A flagpole, as depicted in its original form 𠁩. Based on archaeological evidence, the middle box has been interpreted as a drum (建鼓).

丶.text: A small fire on a torch, when used as the original form of 主.

丸.text: Ideogram (指事), differentiated form of 夗, which was originally the same character.

丹.text: Pictogram (象形) of a well or mine with cinnabar inside. It can also indicate "red cinnabar" used in dyeing clothes (e.g., 彤).

主.text: Three distinct forms can be observed in ancient scripts, all of which have merged into the same character in modern script:.

久.text: Used interchangeably with 氒 in oracle bone script. Likely a pictogram (象形) of an arrow tip.

乏.text: Chen Jian suggests that the graph derives from ⿱口⿰止止, an ideogram shared by 範 and 圍: one 止 was omitted, and one stroke was slanted to avoid confusion with 正.

乗.text: A person 大 climbing a tree 木, with the feet visible. Etymology clearer in alternative form 椉.

九.text: A stylized hand, with bent wrist/forearm (hence the hook stroke at lower right). Earlier forms resemble 手, 寸.

乳.text: A kneeling woman holding and breastfeeding a child. The woman resembles the character 母.

了.text: According to the Shuowen Jiezi, a pictogram (象形) of a baby without arms. The Shuowen defines 了 as "the crossing of lower legs".

争.text: Two hands on a plowshare. The two hands are still visibile on top of the character (爪 and 彐), while the plowshare looks like a vertical hook in modern writing.

二.text: Two parallel strokes. Duplication of 一 (“one”).

五.text: Originally written 𠄡, consisting of 㐅 with a bar on the top and bottom. Original meaning is unclear.

井.text: A square well, with supports on four sides.

亠.text: A couvercle with a handle on top. However, in some characters it is actually a false friend:.

交.text: A human with crossed legs. In today's writing, the upper part of the human is similar to 立, which in turn depicts a man standing.

人.text: Side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg.

亻.text: Side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg.

𠆢.text: Side view of a standing man, highlighting an arm and a leg.

今.text: An inverted 曰 ("to speak"), hence 亼 with a horizontal stroke at the bottom, so the inverted mouth means "not to speak".

components.gloss: a person engaged in an official position

仕.text: It is mainly used as a verb meaning "to serve.".

付.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 亻 (“person”) + 又 (“hand”) or ideogrammic compound (會意): 亻 (“person”) + 寸 (“hand”) – to deliver, to give to someone.

以.text: A person (人) carrying something. It is often simplified to 㠯 in pre-Qin ancient scripts.

任.text: To carry on a shoulder pole.

休.text: A man leaning against a tree, resting.

会.text: 𡆧 is the original form of 𨭗 (“ironware”).

位.text: Often simply written as 立 in idiomatic expressions such as 即位 in Western Zhou inscriptions.

何.text: In the oracle bone script, a pictogram (象形): a man carrying something on their shoulder – the original form of 荷 (“to carry”).

使.text: However, the phonetic component should add part of the meaning since it represents a hand holding perhaps a flag to mean "representative, ambassador".

候.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 亻 + phonetic 矦, as 𠊱. The 矦 component (modified so that ⺈ becomes 乛 on top and 丿 at left becomes 丨) is an ancient form of 侯.

値.text: The character originally conveyed the meaning of "to stand upright." Associated with the character 直, it meant "to hit" or "to be correct," and by extension, it came to mean "value" or "worth.".

儿.text: A standing person. A radical form of 人.

元.text: A figure with two lines 上 for a head (one connected to body, one above it), emphasizing the head.

光.text: Fire over a person's head, emphasizing the shining of light (Shuowen).

全.text: A whole piece of jade; pure jade.

八.text: Two bent lines indicating the original meaning of "to divide". This character is later borrowed to mean "eight" because of homonymy, making the original meaning obsolete (now represented by 分 and 別).

六.text: Perhaps a shed. Originally using the similar-sounding word 廬 (“shed, cabin”) to represent the concept “six” (Liu Xinglong).

兵.text: A pair of hands holding a weapon. Unrelated to 丘.

冂.text: According to Shuowen Jiezi, pictogram composed by three lines that represent a territory outside the city walls and its nearby villages and green fields, a territory that belongs to the uncontaminated countryside, distant from every kind of civilization.

内.text: Simplified from 內. Ideogrammic compound (會意): semantic 入 (“to enter”) + semantic 冂 (“house”).

円.text: The interior 口 is 〇, which is the original ideogram for the word "circle"; 鼎 and 囗 were added later.

最.text: Originally 㝡, phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 取 – "to gather". Later 二 was added as distinguishing marks to disambiguate the character for the meaning "the most".

冠.text: A hand putting a hat on the head.

冫.text: Radical form of 仌, in which the two blocks of ice appear compressed and stylized. Unrelated to 氵, 次, and 准.

冬.text: Unclear. One hypothesis derives 冬 from the antenna-like upper part of an oracle-bone graph formerly read as 鼉 (“crocodilian”) (e.g. 合集 6163反, 7405反), but reinterpreted as 螽 (“katydid; locust”).

几.text: A small stool viewed from the side. The original version was 𠀃, in which the horizontal stroke at the bottom represents the floor and/or the ground.

凡.text: Origin unknown. It consists of two vertical strokes of unequal length.

凶.text: Pictogram (象形) and/or Ideogram (指事)- with the '凵' component representing a hole in the ground and with the '㐅' component (if an ideogram) indicating the existence of a hole and/or (if a pictogram) representing rock, mud, stone or bamboo in the hole. Alternately, could be derived from the upper component of '㚇'.

出.text: To step out of a cave; to exit.

刀.text: A knife. The original form was 𠚣, which can be found in a variant of 利, 𥝢 (in turn used on the top of the character 黎).

⺉.text: A knife. The original form was 𠚣, which can be found in a variant of 利, 𥝢 (in turn used on the top of the character 黎).

初.text: Start making clothes by cutting the cloth.

別.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 冎 (“bone”) + 刂 (“knife”), hence 𠛰 – to cut up bone and flesh. Later, the character was stylized as 別.

利.text: To reap grain (禾) with a knife (刀).

券.text: Contract. Ancient contracts were cut in half.

前.text: Originally 歬, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 止 (“foot”) + 舟 (“boat”) – a foot on a boat moving forward.

力.text: Alternative interpretation, either an arm bending out from the side of the body, or a wooden plough.

加.text: Shuowen: ideogrammic compound (會意): 力 (“strength”) + 口 (“mouth”) – exaggerate; slander.

動.text: However, the phonetic component is a reference to a heavy bag ready to be moved by a human being.

勹.text: A person bending over. In 包, it represents the placenta around a fetus 巳.

包.text: A fetus (巳) in the womb (勹), or a swaddled baby. Shuowen gives both interpretations.

匕.text: A spoon. Unrelated to 老, in which it represents a walking cane.

化.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意) of two 人 (“person”), one upright (亻) and one upside down (𠤎) – reversal; change. Shuowen also considers 𠤎 to be a phonetic component.

北.text: Two men back to back. Originally meaning “back”; the character 背 refers to the original word.

匠.text: Traditionally thought to be an ideogrammic compound (會意): 匚 (“box”) + 斤 (“axe”) (e.g. Shuowen).

十.text: In oracle-bone script, 十 is mostly written as a single vertical stroke; a few examples add a central dot, as in HJ 9204. Later forms added 一, making a cross.

千.text: The Old Chinese pronunciations of 千 and 人 were similar. For the component 人, compare its combining form 亻.

午.text: A pestle (now written 杵). Unrelated to 干.

半.text: To cut a cow into two halves.

協.text: A variant form of 劦 with a phonetic 十 added.

南.text: The oracle-bone form depicts a lidded 同 (“tube; cylindrical vessel”). Some forms contain strokes inside the vessel, probably representing its contents.

単.text: Pictogram (象形) of a war or hunting weapon, a Y-shaped wooden stick with two stones attached on top. The component in the middle in some oracle bones was a huge point which represented a rope around the stick; perhaps, this weapon was used as a spear and then retrieved through this rope.

卜.text: Perhaps a pictogram (象形) of a crack in an oracle bone, used for divination in ancient China.

卩.text: A kneeling person from sideview. Similar but unrelated to 欠, in which the person kneeling has the mouth open, and 女, in which the kneeling figure is a woman.

印.text: A hand suppressing a kneeling person.

components.gloss: person on a cliff or mountain

厚.text: According to Shuowen, 𣆪 is an inverted 亯.

原.text: A spring bursting from a cliff-side – origin. A conservative variant is 厡, in which water is well visible at the bottom.

厳.text: The original script of 譀 (“exaggerated and absurd words”).

去.text: Top figure simplified to 土, unrelated to 士 (“scholar, gentleman”), while bottom simplified to 厶; a conservative variant is 厺.

反.text: The character originally depicted the action of turning the palm of the hand, and by extension, it came to mean "to return" or "to reverse.".

取.text: To take the ear of fallen prey, a rite of hunters mentioned in the Rites of Zhou.

受.text: Possibly a ideogrammic compound (會意): 爪 (“hand”) + 舟 (“boat”) + 又 (“hand”) – to hand over.

古.text: A shield (甲, contraction of 盾 and similar but unrelated to 中) and the radical of the mouth (口) both as a distinguishing mark and as a component that partly indicates pronunciation. Together, they indicate the concept of "strong, firm" (as strong as a shield); original form of 固 (Qiu Xigui, Ding Shan 丁山).

可.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 口 + phonetic 丂 with a reference to exhaled air. Perhaps its original meaning was "to sing", then 訶 and 哥 (可 written twice).

台.text: Its exact structure changes depending on region and time period, but for most of its existence it has been a phono-semantic compound (形聲). The phonetic has always been 之 or 止.

史.text: 又 (“hand”) holding a stylized flag almost identical to 中 perhaps to indicate a representative or ambassador (see its variant 吏 used in 使 to mean "ambassador"). As an alternative, it holds either a pen or a hunting weapon resembling similar to 中.

右.text: Originally written as 又 as a phonetic loan in the oracle bone script; in bronze inscriptions, a meaningless 口 component was added as a distinguishing mark.

号.text: Originally an ideogram (指事) of a tiger with a line representing exhaled air while roaring, thus meaning "to roar; to shout". Later forms added 口 (“mouth”) or 言 (“speech”) to emphasize the act of crying or calling.

各.text: To come, to enter; original form of 𢓜 and 格. The mouth could be referred to the entrance of a cavern or building (see 高, 去 and 谷; however, this is not the case in 向).

吉.text: Originally 圭 and 口 in the oracle bone script. The top component mutated into 士 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions.

同.text: A pipe – original form of 筒.

名.text: To say one's own name to identify oneself in the dark.

向.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 宀 (“house”) + 口 (“mouth”), echos in a place. The original form of 響.

周.text: Oracle bone script: Pictogram (象形): a jade artifact with carved patterns. Original form of 彫 (“to carve”).

呼.text: To exhale, call, or shout from the mouth.

品.text: Triplication of 口, representing various objects. Also occurs in 區.

商.text: The formation is unclear. The base component is consistently 丙; late-period variants add 口 below.

善.text: Originally written 譱 in bronze inscriptions, consisting of two 言 and one 羊. The 言 might have served as the phonetic component, while 羊 represented the sense "good; beautiful" (see 祥, 義).

営.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): abbreviated phonetic 熒 + abbreviated semantic 宮 (“palace”), depicting a person working all night with a light on his house.

器.text: Uncertain. The classical interpretation is an ideogrammic compound (會意): a 犬 (“dog”) guarding four 口 (“vessels”).

囗.text: Pictogram of a square-shaped enclosure. Unrelated to 口 (open mouth) and most likely unrelated to the original version of 丁 (head of a nail).

土.text: Pictogram 象形: a mound of earth. In oracle-bone inscriptions, it could also refer to the soil deity, serving as the original graph of 社.

型.text: An earthen mold, hence form, pattern.

堪.text: Originally meaning “heavy mountain/earthen protrusion”, it later came to signify the act of “enduring” that earth's weight.

報.text: To convict; to punish; to declare guilty.

増.text: Things grow in the earth, to build from earth.

士.text: A war axe. Later, it took the meaning of "soldier" and eventually "officer, intellectual".

声.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 殸 + semantic 耳 (“ear”) and ideogramic compound—an ear hearing a chime being struck.

売.text: Originally 𧷓, an ideogrammic compound (會意) and phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 出 (“go out”) + phonetic 買 (“buy”).

夂.text: Pictogram (象形) of a footprint pointing down. See 夊, which represents a variant of this character.

夏.text: Some scholars identify an oracle bone character ideogrammic compound (會意): 日 (“sun”) + 頁 (“head; man”) as this character – a man under the scorching sun; summer. However, it only appears as a diviner's name, making the identification uncertain.

多.text: Two pieces of meat (肉). In the bronze script, 肉 was corrupted into 夕 due to visual similarity, making 多 into a duplication of 夕.

夜.text: 夕 may also serve as another phonetic component.

太.text: A differentiated form of 大 (“big; great”) with a 丶 added to represent 太 (“too big”).

夫.text: A variant form of 大 preserving its original meaning of 夫 (“man”). 大 and 夫 were originally used interchangeably before settling to their current meanings.

央.text: Unclear. Possibly a pictogram (象形) of a man with the neck in shackles – original form of 鞅.

失.text: Pictogram (象形) depicting a footprint of someone that has fallen surrounded by drops of blood.

奏.text: Two hands (廾) holding an object, perhaps a musical instrument used during a sacrifical ritual (the lower part of the object originally was similar to 夲).

女.text: A woman with folded arms kneeling or standing.

委.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 禾 + semantic 女 (in the oracle bones inscriptions, there was 𠃊 instead of a woman kneeling).

子.text: An image of a baby, with a large head and spread arms. The legs are wrapped in a blanket.

components.gloss: an old man with long hair, bent over

孝.text: An old man and a child, filial piety between generations.

学.text: The earliest oracle bone form consists of 𦥑 (“two hands”) + 六 (“building”); subsequent groups write 爻 (“counting rods”) + 六 or 𦥑 + 爻, and later forms combine all three into 𦥯 (𦥑 + 爻 + 六), with some abbreviated to 爻. Bronze inscriptions add semantic 子 (“child”).

宀.text: A house; similar to 广. According to Wang Yun (王筠), the latter character depicts a building with three walls, while the former depicts a house with four walls.

守.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 宀 (“roof; building”) + 寸 (“hand”); to guard, keep, or defend a place (e.g., a building whose roof is visible on top of the character). It's possible that 寸 (original form of 肘) is also a phonetic component.

安.text: 安 is the original character of 安坐 (“to sit at ease”).

官.text: Compositionally related to 宮, but approximately analysable as ideogrammic compound (會意): 宀 + 𠂤 – multiple rooms under a roof, an official building.

家.text: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 𢑓 (“male pig”). An archaic variant closer to the original drawing is 𡩀.

審.text: There are two theories about the component 田. One is that it was originally 口 (“mouth”), then corrupted into 曰 (“say”), then further into 田.

寸.text: Two separate characters with this form exist:.

寺.text: To grasp, to hold. Phonetic 𡳿 (之), which represents a footprint pointing up, became 土 or 士 in the clerical script from the late Western Han to the Eastern Han, and semantic 又 became 寸 in Small Seal Script.

対.text: In the oracle bone and bronze scripts, it was an ideogrammic compound (會意): 丵 (“tool for digging”) + 土 (“earth”) + 又 (“hand”). The original meaning of the character is unclear, but it may be “to develop (land)”.

専.text: A hand turning a spindle or spinning wheel. It has come to mean to bundle several things together into one.

射.text: In the oracle bone script, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 弓 (“bow”) + 矢 (“arrow”) – to shoot a bow. In the bronze inscriptions, a hand (又) drawing the bowstring was added.

尊.text: Shuowen: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 酋 (“wine”) + 寸 (“hand”) – a hand 寸 offering a vessel of wine 酋 to show respect and veneration.

少.text: Four dots, perhaps three grains of sand (see 沙), to indicate "a few, a little". Phonetically borrowed from 小 (“small”), which is depicted by three dots.

尢.text: Ideogram (指事), a man with bent legs (jumping or collapsing).

就.text: Originally 𫢁, ideogrammic compound (會意): 享 + 京, a temple and a tower – meaning "to sacrifice at a high place". During the Warring States period, 享 was omitted.

尸.text: A man with his legs bending, and a side to the front. Its ancient form is 𡰣.

展.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 尸 + abbreviated phonetic 𧝑, which has a variant 𧝣; the original version is 㞡.

山.text: Three mountain peaks. In the Oracle Bone Script, they were represented by triangles rather than vertical strokes.

岸.text: The edge of the land. Its proto-form was 屵.

川.text: Pictogram (象形) of flowing water – compare 水, 巛, and 𡿧.

工.text: A bladed tool to plow the ground and to mark a border. As an alternative, a carpenter's square; according to the second interpretation, the character is related to the original meaning of 巨.

左.text: Originally written 𠂇 and 䶹 in the oracle bone script: Pictogram (象形) – a left hand.

差.text: To hull wheat by rubbing grains inside hands. Original form of 搓 (“to rub with hands; to scrub; to twist”).

己.text: Silk rope for binding objects. Original form of 紀.

巻.text: To bend; reel of books. The phonetic component could also add part of the meaning since it indicates the act of rolling rice into balls, hence "bending" rice.

市.text: Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 兮 (“bustling”) + phonetic 之.

席.text: A woven mat with ornament. Later, a phonetic 石 was added and the image of the mat corrupted into 巾 (“cloth”).

帰.text: To eradicate the enemy and return.

干.text: Pictogram (象形) of a shield with feather ornaments on top; in some versions in oracle bones, the central and flat part of the shield can be seen as 回.

年.text: Originally meaning "harvest", it later came to mean "year". In the oracle bone script and early bronze inscriptions, it was originally written like 秂.

幹.text: Originally 榦, a phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 倝 + semantic 木 (“tree”). The semantic 木 was replaced with a phonetic 干, making both components phonetic.

幻.text: Jiajie (假借), but of what is unclear:.

幼.text: 幺 may also act as a phonetic component.

广.text: A house with a roof, similar to 宀. According to Wang Yun (王筠), the former character depicts a building with three walls, while the latter depicts a house with four walls.

components.gloss: house built to depend on a cliff

度.text: Duan Yucai argues that the presence of the hand component in this character is because the hand was used as a reference for measurement. 石 is then corrupted into 𲟁.

廴.text: Pictogram (象形) – a man (人) with one leg behind him, implying a stride/step. Unrelated to 乃.

延.text: Originally 㢟, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 彳 (“walking”) + 止 (“foot”) – "to travel far". The stroke at the top started being added as a distinguishing mark at the end of the Warring States period, as a way to distinguish its usage from 㢟 as an adverb to mean "prolonged", making it an Ideogram (指事).

建.text: Originally, a pictogram (象形) – a hand (又) planting a pole (𰀁) into a base. The left component was originally written as ∟.

弊.text: Emphatic form of 敝 – destroying something with both hands.

弋.text: A sharp peg – original form of 杙 (“peg”). Same as 才 and 尗.

強.text: A Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 虫 and phonetic 𪪺.

影.text: The original meaning is "shadow". The phonetic component also indicates the concept of image.

彳.text: Simplified from 行 – the left side of the character, which represents a street intersection as seen from above.

役.text: The character originally depicted guarding a border with a weapon in hand, and by extension, it came to represent the idea of performing a duty or task.

後.text: In oracle bone script, ideogrammic compound (會意): 幺 (“thread”) + 夊 (“foot”) – a foot bound by a rope, thus lagging behind. The component 彳 was added afterwards to emphasize this action.

従.text: Originally written as 从. Now phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 辵 (“walk”) + phonetic 从 (“follow”).

必.text: Likely a pictogram (象形) – the handle (⿻⿺㇂丶丿) found on the right hand side of weapons such as 戊 or 戈 or 戉 written stand-alone. Two decorative strokes were then added to the sides.

念.text: Zhang (2021): Ideogrammic compound (會意): 亼 (“upside-down mouth”) + 心 (“heart”): to listen to one's heart. Original character for 念 (“to think”).

思.text: Original form was 恖, considered by Shuowen to be a phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 囟 + semantic 心 (“heart”). It may also be a ideogrammic compound (會意): 囟 (“fontanel”) + 心 (“heart”).

性.text: Nature, personal quality, hence of the heart.

意.text: Modern form is a compound of 音 and 心 (“heart”). However, the top component is etymologically unrelated to 音.

愛.text: Originally written as 㤅. Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 旡 + semantic 心 (“heart”).

慶.text: In oracle bone inscriptions Ideogrammic compound (會意): 廌 (“antelope”) + 心. The component 心 signified goodness, blessings and auspiciousness.

components.gloss: a form of punishment involving tattooing the eyes

憲.text: The character conveys the meaning of "law" or "rule.".

戈.text: Pictogram (象形) ― an ancient weapon with a single blade. The vertical handle developed into the long upper-left to lower-right diagonal stroke.

成.text: The phonetic component is not 囗 or 口, as folk etymology states. According to Ji Xusheng 季旭昇, its original meaning was "city walls", with a reference to something protected conveyed by the weapon.

我.text: A pictogram (象形) of a trident-like weapon or tool (note the oracle bone script form 𢦐). conjecture about its similarity to a kind of three-bladed polearm found at archaeological sites. It was already borrowed for sound as an instance of jiajie (假借) for the pronoun 我 (“I”) since the oracle bone script.

戒.text: To hold up a weapon as warning.

戸.text: One-half of 門 (“gate”). The character in its original form is similar to 𠁣.

戻.text: A dog 犬 bending to enter through a door 戶 – to bend over. Extended to mean crooked, deviant, contrary.

所.text: The sound of logging (the definition given in Shuowen).

手.text: Hand and fingers. The top stroke is the bent over middle finger, while the horizontal strokes are each two fingers.

扌.text: Hand and fingers. The top stroke is the bent over middle finger, while the horizontal strokes are each two fingers.

抱.text: Hold in one’s hands. Note that 包 has the meaning of “wrap”, hence connotations of “wrap in one’s hands, embrace”, thereby also making it an ideogrammic compound.

撃.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 手 (“hand”) + phonetic 毄, probably reinforced by the "hit against" semantics of 毄 – to strike with the hand.

攵.text: A hand (又) holding a tool of some sort (possibly a weapon or whip), meaning “to hit”. The tool later corrupted into the phonetic component 卜.

改.text: In the oracle bone script, a phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 巳 + semantic 攴.

components.gloss: hand holding a tool or weapon
teaching cane; stick that represents authority

文.text: A man with a painted or tattooed chest – original form of 紋. The tattoo was usually a cross, a V shape or a stylized heart.

斉.text: Multiple neatly arranged fruits or thorns. The oracle bone script of 櫅 depicts these growing on a tree.

斗.text: Pictogram (象形) (Shuowen), indicating a ladle-shaped dipper or cup used to measure grain (see below) held by hand.

斜.text: The character expresses the idea of scooping or drawing out. By extension, it is also used to mean "slant" or "diagonal.".

新.text: To chop wood. Original form of 薪 (“firewood”).

方.text: Possibly the original character of 旁 (“side”), with its form related to 巫. 巫 depicts four extremities with indicator symbols, being the original character of 荒 in 四荒.

旋.text: 〇 is the original form of 圓 and also serves as a phonetic component. It has since merged with the 止 into the unrelated 疋.

日.text: The sun. A dot or line was added in the centre to distinguish it from visually similar characters, e.g. 口.

早.text: Early bronze inscriptions: Pictogram (象形) – acorn. Original form of 皂 through an intermediate variant 皁 (once also written as 草).

明.text: The sun just rising and the moon not yet set – dawn (天明). In the oracle bone script it is mostly "daybreak"; a few instances mean "sight" or are a place name.

易.text: Oracle bone script and bronze inscriptions: a pictogram (象形) of a filled container, the original form of 賜 (“to confer, to bestow”). Possibly specialised from 益 (“to increase, to add”).

星.text: 晶 originally referred to this word; a phonetic 生 was added later (Ji Xusheng, 2004). 晶 was later simplified into 日.

春.text: Some oracle-bone and bronze forms contain only two components, either 艸/屮/木 with 屯, or 日 with 屯. The character may relate to a semantic cluster of its phonetic series: 蠢 (“to stir”), 純 (“pure, unmixed”), 敦 (“round”), and 芚 (“to sprout”).

昨.text: However, the phonetic component could add part of the meaning since it was borrowed phonetically to mean "at first".

晴.text: Written as 夝 in Shuowen and as 星 in the Classic of Poetry.

曰.text: A mouth (口) with word or breath (一) coming out. Unrelated to 甘.

月.text: Pictographic representation of a crescent moon. Related to 夕 and interchangeable in the past, but both are unrelated to 多, in which it represents two pieces of meat stylized as 夕.

有.text: The hand shape has been abstracted to 𠂇; compare 右, where 又 has also taken this shape. The 肉 in turn has taken the form of ⺼.

望.text: Originally written 𦣠, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 臣 (“eye”) + 𡈼 (“person standing on the ground”) – a person standing up and looking off into the distance. Later 月 (“moon”) was added to produce 朢.

朝.text: In the oracle bone script, it was an ideogrammic compound (會意): 2 or 4 屮 (“grass”) or even 木 (“tree”) + 日 (“sun”) + 月 (“moon”) – the sun rising above the ground while the waning moon is still in the sky – the morning.

木.text: A tree: branches on top, roots on the bottom (more visible in earlier forms).

末.text: A tree (木) with its top highlighted with an extra stroke, implying the meaning of “apex”; contrast 本, 朱.

本.text: A tree (木) with its bottom highlighted with an extra stroke, accentuating the roots; contrast 末, 朱.

条.text: Originally it indicates a small branch, perhaps with some reference to a wooden stick (in the top component, there is a man warned by a hand holding a vertical stick). The bottom part of the character is unrelated to 茶.

来.text: Pictogram (象形) of wheat – original character of 麥 (“wheat”) or 麳 (“wheat”). The line in the middle represents the ear, the two lines pointing upwards represent leaves, and the lines pointing downwards represent the stem and roots.

東.text: A pictogram of a full 橐 (“bag”) tied at both ends. It is the original form of 重: forms with a human figure gave rise to 重, while forms without it gave rise to 東.

林.text: Duplication of 木 (“tree”) to give the idea of multiple trees (compare 森), thus a forest.

果.text: Fruits on a tree. Related to the original form of 采.

査.text: It represents the idea of a raft made from assembled wood. The original character is 楂.

核.text: A kind of tree. Modern meanings are borrowed.

森.text: Triplication of 木 (“tree”), to suggest a large number (compare 三) of trees such as one would find in a forest.

楽.text: Strings on a piece of wood, i.e. a wooden musical instrument.

権.text: A type of tree named 黃華 (Shuowen); phonetically borrowed for "standard weight".

次.text: A person exhaling. Possibly the original form of 咨 (“to sigh”).

止.text: A footprint pointing up, originally meaning "foot"; stylized as 龰. The derivative 趾 refers to the original meaning.

武.text: Army going on an expedition. In the character 武, the 戈 component is written above the 止 component.

歩.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 止 (“foot”) + 止 (“foot”) reversed – one foot in front of the other. Unrelated to 少.

歯.text: A mouth full of teeth. Now phono-semantic compound (形聲) with phonetic 止 added.

殳.text: Pictogram (象形) or Ideogrammic compound (會意): 𠘧 + 又 – a hand holding a tool similar to a hammer, hence activity (with a reference to the act of "beating").

段.text: In the bronze script it is a phono-semantic compound (形聲) and ideogrammic compound (會意): phonetic 厂 + semantic 殳, showing a hammer in hand breaking a stone with fragments coming off; 殳 was the pictogram of a hammer and later was borrowed to indicate a bamboo halberd. Most of the character is identical to 叚.

殺.text: In the oracle bone script, it was an ideogrammic compound (會意) of a boar that had been impaled in the head.

殿.text: Shuowen: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 𡱂 + semantic 殳 (“hand holding a weapon”) – the sound of hitting (not attested in ancient documents).

毋.text: In the oracle bone script, 母 (“mother”) was borrowed to represent this character. It was later specialized to distinguish it from “mother”, replacing the two dots with one stroke.

母.text: Differentiated form of 女 with the addition of distinguishing dots. In the early oracle bone texts both words 女 (“woman”) and 母 were written as 女 (,, ).

毎.text: Possibly an ideogrammic compound (會意) and phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 屮 + phonetic 母 (“woman”). The top component resembling 屮 may represent a bamboo hairpin (笄) to indicate that the woman was at least 15 years old.

毒.text: Chen, Jian (2020): Pictogram (象形) of a woman wearing a feathered ornament on her head – original form of 纛 (“feathered ornament”). Later borrowed for 毒 (“poison”).

比.text: Chu Wan-li (1948): Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 匕 + phonetic 匕.

水.text: Pictogram (象形) of water flowing; sometimes written as the variant 氺 (e.g., 泰, 录, and 黎). Next to a character, it is compressed and stylized into 氵 (which is unrelated to 冫).

氵.text: Pictogram (象形) of water flowing; sometimes written as the variant 氺 (e.g., 泰, 录, and 黎). Next to a character, it is compressed and stylized into 氵 (which is unrelated to 冫).

氺.text: Pictogram (象形) of water flowing; sometimes written as the variant 氺 (e.g., 泰, 录, and 黎). Next to a character, it is compressed and stylized into 氵 (which is unrelated to 冫).

求.text: Pictogram (象形) of a centipede. Original form of 蛷.

汽.text: Also ideogrammic compound 氵 (water) and 气 (air), representing water in air form.

泉.text: Pictogram (象形) or ideogrammic compound (會意): 白 (“spring mouth”) + 水 (“water”) – water flowing from the source of a spring.

components.gloss: a type of antelope or caprid

活.text: The 𠯑 later transformed into 舌; a conservative variant is 𣴠.

派.text: 𠂢 is the original pictogram for this character; 水 was added later to differentiate.

減.text: To seal off a stream of water, decreasing its flow. 咸 is the original character of 緘 and also serves as a semantic component.

火.text: Pictographic representation of a fire. Written as 灬 when at the bottom of a character, but still seen in the original form in the character 灸.

灬.text: Pictographic representation of a fire. Written as 灬 when at the bottom of a character, but still seen in the original form in the character 灸.

無.text: A person dancing with ox tails held in both hands to pray for rain.

然.text: To burn. The derivative 燃 preserves the original word.

燃.text: Burn with fire. Originally 然, but because it was phonetically borrowed for abstract senses, 火 was added for differentiation.

父.text: A hand holding a stone blade, referring to a man working with a stone axe.

片.text: Mirror image of 爿 (“piece”), which is the pictogram of a bed.

牛.text: Pictogram (象形) of a bull's head, with two horns and two ears. Perhaps unrelated to 告; unrelated to 先.

犬.text: The side view of a dog.

犭.text: The side view of a dog.

狂.text: The latter is the ancient form of 往 (“to go”).

玄.text: Ideogram (指事), two interwoven threads 幺 and a distinguishing mark 亠 on top. The whole character should represent a rope, as seen in 率 and 弦.

率.text: According to Xu Shen, a net to capture birds. 冫幺冫is the net, and the top and bottom is the stick.

玉.text: The character's shape was historically very similar to 王; a dot was introduced to differentiate the two.

王.text: Pictogram (象形) of a ritual axe made perhaps of jade, symbols of the king's power. A ceremonial axe was kept near the throne, and was used for performing rituals in ancient China.

珍.text: Originally meant a rich, robust gemstone (玉), and then also developed the meaning of "rare".

班.text: To cut jade to pieces with knife. The pieces of jade appear as a more conservative version 玨.

瓦.text: Fired earthenware pottery, or a tile.

甘.text: Something sweet in an open mouth; the original drawing is 𠁿. Original form of 含.

用.text: Formed by adding a handle to 同.

田.text: Pictographic representation of a field divided into four sections. See the original version of 甫 and 里.

由.text: Pictogram of new shoots or leaves growing from 木; possibly the original graph of 㽕, with its upper part later extracted as 由.

申.text: A bolt of lightning. Original character of 電 (“lightning”) and 神 (“god; deity; spirit”).

男.text: Man providing the strength for agricultural and/or other kinds of (physical) labour on a field.

画.text: Li Shoukui (2016): Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 聿 (“brush”) + phonetic 規. 規 (“compass”) appears in the oracle bone script in its pictographic protoform resembling a 乂.

components.gloss: rope tying the bag of feed

畜.text: A bag of feed, hence livestock.

略.text: To walk around a field (to outline it).

疋.text: A foot 止 with a leg/thigh on top; the pictogram is similar to 足. Unrelated with the bottom part of 是, which is 止 on oracle bones.

疒.text: A person lying in bed. Original form of 疾 (“illness”).

病.text: Illness. Note that 丙 also means “fire”, hence connotations of “lying feverishly in bed”.

痛.text: The character conveys the meaning of "pain" or "to hurt.".

癶.text: A right and a left foot (止), hence in divergent direction; by contrast, 舛 depicts two feet in convergent direction.

components.gloss: pictogrammic of raised object; stepping stone

登.text: The two hands at the bottom disappeared, but they are retained in the conservative variant 𤼷.

皆.text: Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 虍 + phonetic 几 + semantic 口.

皮.text: A hand (又) stripping the fur from an animal pelt (similar to 革). The pelt moved to the top left and became abstracted.

皿.text: Pictogram (象形) A pictograph of an empty container, such as a chalice. The handles are conjoined in the modern form.

盗.text: In oracle bone script, Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 㳄 + 舟 (“boat”) – an overflowing river. This character is technically a different word than the modern 盜 (“steal”), used interchangeably with 衍 in oracle bones, or as a phonetic loan for 羨, and 延 in bronze script.

盟.text: Oracle bone script (𥁰): Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 囧 + phonetic 皿.

components.gloss: a person with an emphasized eye

監.text: A person looking into a container. Original form of 鑑 (“mirror”).

直.text: Oracle bone script: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 目 (“eye”) + 丨 (“?”).

省.text: Originally 眚. In oracle bone script, an phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 生 + 目 (“eye”) – "to inspect".

看.text: To put a hand above eyes to gaze afar.

県.text: To hang with the string 糸 by the head 目 (using an eye to represent a head) on a tree 木. Originally referred to 懸 (“to hang”); later jiajie (假借) for 縣 (“administrative division”).

眠.text: Close your eyes and go to sleep.

督.text: To look over, to oversee (with eyes).

矢.text: An arrow. More recognizable in older forms.

知.text: Originally the same character as 智, used interchangeably. In oracle bone inscriptions, ideogrammic compound (會意): 大 (“adult”) + 口 (“mouth”) + 子 (“child”) – to transmit knowledge.

矯.text: To straighten; to make as straight as an arrow shaft.

石.text: Representation of a qing (磬). 口 was subsequently added as a decorative element.

砂.text: Originally, this character was a variant form of 沙, a Pictogram (象形) that represents the appearance of sand along a riverbank.

確.text: Rock-solid, as certain as a rock.

示.text: An altar. The original form is similar to unrelated character 丅, and additional strokes are added to prevent confusion with an ancient variant of 下 and the ancient version of 主.

礻.text: An altar. The original form is similar to unrelated character 丅, and additional strokes are added to prevent confusion with an ancient variant of 下 and the ancient version of 主.

祖.text: Specialization of 且. See there for more.

票.text: Simplified from 𤐫. Ideogrammic compound (會意): semantic 火 (“fire”) + semantic 𢍱 (“to rise high”), which represents two pairs of hands holding and rising an object, perhaps a bag or basket (西).

祭.text: The hand offers a piece of meat at the altar during a ceremony.

禾.text: Picture of a plant stalk. The stalk is more recognizable in older form.

私.text: 厶 originally referred to this word, 禾 was added later.

秋.text: The oracle bone forms and bronze inscriptions show the pictogram (象形) of a cricket or a locust, sometimes with a fire 火 glyph underneath. In its later form, became a Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 禾 (“grain”) + abbreviated phonetic 𤒅.

税.text: Simplified from 稅. Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 禾 + phonetic 兑.

穴.text: Pictogram (象形)—possibly an entrance to a cave or a door flap. A conservative version is 𠕉.

突.text: Shuowen: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 穴 (“cave; den”) + 犬 (“dog”) – a dog suddenly coming out of a den.

窃.text: In the Warring States period, the character existed in the forms 𢿑 and 𱡡; the latter of which is likely the ancestor of the modern form, a Phono-semantic compound (形聲): 米 (“rice”) + 攴 (“action”) + phonetic 禼 – theft.

窯.text: It represents a hole used for firing pottery, which is a pottery kiln.

立.text: A person standing on the ground; compare 大 and 文.

競.text: According to Shuowen, an Ideogrammic compound (會意): 誩 (“argument”) + 儿 (“man”) + 儿 (“man”) – two individuals debating vigorously. Also possibly a Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 誩 + semantic 儿 (“man”) + semantic 儿 (“man”).

竹.text: Two bamboo stalks, with leaves. Earlier forms resembled 个 + 个, current form resembles rather ケ + ケ, or 亇 + 亇.

⺮.text: Two bamboo stalks, with leaves. Earlier forms resembled 个 + 个, current form resembles rather ケ + ケ, or 亇 + 亇.

笑.text: Originally phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 艸 (“grass”) + semantic 犬 (“dog”). Later, phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 竹 + phonetic 夭.

第.text: 竹 here refers to the bamboo strips used for writing (e.g. accounting, classification) in ancient times.

筆.text: 聿 originally referred to this word; 竹 was added later to differentiate.

答.text: Originally, it was a variant of 荅, where the semantic component 艸 (grass) was later mistakenly replaced by 竹 (bamboo). It expresses the meaning of "to respond.".

算.text: In current form, 竹 (“bamboo”) + 目 + 廾.

米.text: Rice kernels without husk. The character 粟, by contrast, refers to rice kernels with husk.

細.text: The right component is etymologically unrelated to 田 in which it was corrupted to after the Han dynasty.

終.text: Originally a pictogram (象形), 夂 (definition 2) – the knot at the end of a cord. Later reformulated as a phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 糹 + phonetic 冬.

絶.text: Originally ideogrammic compound (會意): 刀 (“knife”) + 幺 (“silk”) or ideogrammic compound (會意): 刀 (“knife”) + 𢆶 (“silk”) – to cut silk threads.

編.text: To knit together a book (with thread).

罪.text: The original version is 𦋛 and its original meaning was a net for fishing, then used instead of 辠 due to the similarity of the latter character to 皇, which represents the Emperor.

美.text: A person (大) wearing a headdress (now written 羊) of feathers or ram's horn.

義.text: The component 羊 here signifies "good; beautiful; auspicious" and not "sheep". See 祥, 善 and 幸.

習.text: To learn to fly, to practice flying.

老.text: A man with long hair (an old man), leaning on a cane.

components.gloss: an old man with long hair, bent over

考.text: Variant of 老 – Ideogrammic compound (會意): 耂 (“an old man with long hair, bent over”) + 丂 (“a walking cane”) originally drawn as 匕 – an old man, leaning on a cane.

者.text: A sugarcane with full stems, with some points around (either leaves or drops of sweet liquid) and an open and smiling mouth at the bottom. This is the original character for either 蔗 (“sugarcane”) or 煮 (“to boil”).

聴.text: Originally 𦔻, hence ideogrammic compound (會意): 耳 (“ear”) + 口 (“mouth(s)”) – to listen.

肉.text: Ribs of an animal’s torso or simply a physical representation of a slice of meat. Stylized into 月 when next to a phonetic component and 𱼀 and/or 夕 inside some characters.

肩.text: The component 戶 (representing the shape of a shoulder) is combined with 月 (the radical of 肉, meaning "flesh" or "meat") to convey the meaning of "shoulder.".

育.text: Evolved geometrically from 胄 in Han dynasty era.

能.text: A bear. In the character, two paws are visible as a pair of 匕 and the face with the open mouth is stylized as 月.

脳.text: Originally 匘, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 匕 + 巛 (“hair”) + 囟 (“head; fontanel”). 匕 was later replaced with 肉 (“flesh”).

臣.text: A vertical eye of a man looking downwards. As an individual character it has taken on the meanings “slave; servant; minister”, while the meaning relating to eyes appears when used as a radical, such as in 臨 (“to look down at”) and 監 (“to inspect”).

臨.text: A person looking down at some objects.

自.text: A nose – original form of 鼻 (“nose”). Later phonetically borrowed as an instance of jiajie (假借) for 自 (“oneself; from”).

臭.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 犬 (“dog”) + 自 (“nose”), referring to the dog's strong sense of smell. Original form of 嗅 (“to smell”).

至.text: An arrow stuck into the ground. Some folk etymologies interpret the whole pictogram as an eagle catching a prey.

臼.text: A mortar. See the original version of 舂, in which a pestle is visible on top.

舌.text: A snake's tongue emerging upwards from a mouth (口).

舛.text: Ideogrammic compound (會意): 夊 + 𡕒 (second character roughly ヰ) – two feet facing in the same direction.

舜.text: Altered from seal script form 䑞.

舞.text: This character was coined to preserve the original meaning of 無, which is "dancing"; hence, the upper component also adds part of the meaning. A conservative variant is 𦨅.

般.text: The proto-form of 盤 + 攴. The proto-form of 盤 was later corrupted into 舟, and 攴 evolved into 殳.

艮.text: A person looking back to introduce the concept of disobedience and/or limit. Similar but unrelated to 見.

良.text: Possibly depicts corridors and a room, in which case it would be the original form of 廊. Unrelated to 食, 艮 and 即.

色.text: It depicts a hand pressing down on a kneeling person. 色 was an ancient form of 印; they both originally meant "to press down", meaning now written with 抑.

花.text: Originally 𠌶 or 華 before the Han dynasty.

若.text: A person combing their hair; obedient.

草.text: Originally referred to 皂, and later borrowed for the “grass” sense, replacing 艸.

葉.text: 枼 is the original pictogram for this word; 艸 was added to differentiate.

葬.text: Bury the dead 死 in the grass 茻. Top is now grass radical (艹), while bottom is simplified to 廾, hence graphically 艹 + 死 + 廾.

衆.text: Variant of 眾, with the top component 罒 replaced by 血, and the bottom component 𫡑 replaced by 乑.

衛.text: Simplified from 䘙. Ideogrammic compound (會意) and phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 行 + phonetic 韋 + semantic 帀.

衣.text: Pictogram (象形) Outline of the chest, upper clothing.

衤.text: Pictogram (象形) Outline of the chest, upper clothing.

表.text: Originally 𧘝, an ideogrammic compound (會意): 衣 (“garment; clothing”) + 毛 (“hair; feather”) – outer garment.

衰.text: A piece of clothing made from palm fibers to be used as a raincoat (original form of 蓑).

裁.text: However, the phonetic component has a reference to a blade and an arrow, hence to the concept of cutting (e.g., fabric).

裕.text: Folk etymology claims 谷 to represent space in the clothes.

襾.text: According to Xu Shen, it is 冂 overlapped with 凵 and a horizontal stroke on top to indicate the act of covering something.

西.text: The oracle-bone forms of 西 fall into two types: open-topped and closed-topped. The open-topped type is found only in periods I–II, especially in the Bin and Chu groups; later scripts inherit the closed-topped type.

要.text: A man 大 then drawn as a woman (女) with two hands pointing to his/her midsection. On top of the character there was huge eye 目, then stylized as a horn 角.

見.text: 目 (“eye”) + 卩 (“kneeling person”) – a kneeling human figure with a large eye for a head. Similar but unrelated to 艮.

規.text: Originally a pictogram (象形): a cross-shaped measuring compass similar to 乂. The protoform also appears as the bottom component in the oracle bone script of 畫.

親.text: Bronze script: phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 辛 + semantic 見 (“see”).

角.text: A horn. A conservative version is 𧢲.

解.text: A knife separates a horn from a cow, i.e. “cut up (an ox)”.

言.text: From 口 and ▽(possibly original form of 弋, marking location). Later: from 口 and 辛 or 䇂 (possibly mixed with 舌).

設.text: 埶 in this character initially appears as an ancient short form ⿰𡉣攴.

話.text: The right component is not related to 舌 (“tongue”).

谷.text: Valley (口) in between two mountain walls represented by near-parallel lines. The original version is 𠔌.

豆.text: Some kind of container. Borrowed phonetically for the plant name.

象.text: Pictographic representation of an elephant. ⺈ represents the trunk, 𫩏 represents the head, and 𧰨 represents the body.

貝.text: Cowrie used as currency in ancient China. Unrelated to the original version of 則.

貧.text: Since the phonetic means "to divide", a possible mnemonic is "to divide one's money".

質.text: Zhu Junsheng also interpret this as a phono-semantic compound (形聲), where he regards 斦 as an original form of 櫍.

赤.text: The color of fire (a person by a fire). The original version is 𤆍.

赦.text: In the bronze script, it was written as 𢼜, a phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 亦 + semantic 攴 (“hand holding a stick”). In later scripts, the phonetic component was replaced with 赤.

走.text: A running man. An additional 止 (“foot”) was added later.

足.text: Pictogram (象形) of a leg; similar to 疋.

身.text: From a pictograph of a pregnant woman. Unrelated to 射.

車.text: Originally a carriage seen from above. In the oracle bone script, there were large wheels on both sides and a central shaft at the front.

軍.text: Semantic 車 (“chariot”) + phonetic 勹. The phonetic component here is not 勹, but the original form of 螾, which also acts as the phonetic component of 旬, 勻 and 云.

軽.text: The word originally referred to a kind of light carriage.

辛.text: Pictogram (象形) Older oracle bone forms of 辛 (⿱∇木) depict newly grown tree shoots, acting as the original ideogram for 新 and 薪. In 新, the top of the axe component (斤) aligns with the bottom of ∇, signifying the chopping of wood.

辞.text: In oracle bone and Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, the left component 𤔔 depicts hands drawing out silk threads with a 壬/工-shaped element at the centre (perhaps a reeling tool or a midpoint marker), representing the act of ordering and sorting silk.

辰.text: A kind of agricultural tool used for tilling the fields and removing weeds (; ), possibly made of a kind of large clam 蜃.

辶.text: A more conservative and obsolete version is 𣥆. The bottom part is now stylized as 龰.

辺.text: Originally 臱. Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 辶 (“walking; movement”) + phonetic 臱.

退.text: In oracle bone script, ideogrammic compound (會意): 皀 (“food vessel”) + 夊 (“downward foot”) – to leave the table after eating. Variants that depicted the vessel as 酉 or 豆 were common.

造.text: Unclear. Generally considered to be unrelated to 告 in its original form.

週.text: Considered a 後起字. Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 辶 (“walking”) + phonetic 周.

進.text: A bird can only walk forward, not backward, hence implying "forward". Shuowen Jiezi interprets it as Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 辵 + abbreviated phonetic 閵.

道.text: First attested in early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions as a 行 (“road”) + 首 (“head”), later augmented with 又 (寸) or 止 in the middle and late periods. The 亍 on the right eventually disappeared, leading to the semantic components combining into 辵 in the seal script.

⻏.text: The bottom part of the radical is unrelated to 巴 and the top component is most likely unrelated to the original version of 丁.

郡.text: It represents one of the ancient local administrative divisions.

部.text: It originally refers to a place in today's Gansu.

酉.text: A wine vessel with a pointed bottom.

酒.text: 酉 is the original pictogram for this word; 水 was added later to distinguish.

里.text: A measure of land and fields; mile; place.

重.text: A man carrying a bag. A glyph 土 (“earth”) was later added to show that the bag-carrying man is standing on the ground.

量.text: Inconclusive. In the oracle bone and bronze scripts, the most common form was 日 (“sun”) + 東 (“bag; east”).

金.text: Semantic 士 or 王, + semantic 呂 (“two blocks of metal”) + phonetic 亼 (今). The blocks of metal were originally drawn as: and later as 丷.

鉄.text: The original version, according to the Shuowen Jiezi, is 𨮯, with 大 on top, hence the original phonetic component should be not 𢧜.

長.text: An old man with long hair; an ancient variant still used is 镸 (e.g., ⾽ and 鬓).

components.gloss: latch and/or wooden pole that shuts a door

開.text: A pair of hands opening a latched door. 一 and 廾 are combined into 开 since the Small Seal script; however, in the conservative variant 𨵑, the two hands and the latch are well visible.

間.text: Variant form of 閒 (“space, gap”) with 月 (“moon”) replaced by 日 (“day”).

関.text: The bronze inscription was in the form of 門 (“door”) + 卝 (“locked door; two wooden sticks to lock a door”). 卝 might also serve as a phonetic component.

阝.text: Pictogram (象形), a row of steps on a hill, still visible in the upper part 𠂤. The original version is 𨸏.

限.text: It conveys the meaning of "limit" or "boundary.".

隹.text: A short‐tailed bird (e.g. a sparrow). In addition to referring to 隹 (“short-tailed bird”), it also is the original form of 鷕 (“cry of a bird”) with the intermediate form 唯.

雅.text: It represents the meaning of a rook, which is a type of crow. By extension, it is used metaphorically to mean "elegant" or "refined.".

集.text: The variant 雧 shows three birds instead.

難.text: A type of bird. Phonetically borrowed for other senses.

雪.text: Ancient simplification of 䨮, which is in turn phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 雨 (“rain”) + phonetic 彗.

雲.text: Originally written 云, with the 雨 radical added to 云 to distinguish from the borrowed sense of “to speak”.

零.text: On the oracle bone script, only thick raindrops are depicted falling from the sky.

雷.text: Ancient simplification of 靁, which was a phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 雨 (“rain”) + phonetic 畾.

電.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 雨 (“rain”) + phonetic 申; also ideogrammic compound (會意): 雨 + 申 (“lightning”).

青.text: Zhang (2022): Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 生 + phonetic 井.

静.text: Note that 青 is also a compound with two phonetic components.

非.text: Two wings facing opposite directions. Originally, it represented wings; then, according to Xu Shen, its meaning changed into "leave; disobey" (違).

面.text: Pictogram (象形), A man’s face, with an eye exaggerated, derived from 𦣻. The horizontal stroke was added later.

革.text: A stretched animal hide: the upper is head, the bottom is the tail and legs. The hands 臼 around the hide were briefly added later.

音.text: Based on the structure of 言, with an additional short horizontal stroke inside the 口 (“mouth”), forming a shape similar to 甘. The Shuowen Jiezi describes the structure as 从言含一 ("from 言 containing 一").

頁.text: Head of a kneeling person, emphasising “head”.

顔.text: Variant form of 顏 (彥 → 彦).

風.text: Jiajie (假借) of 鳳 (“fenghuang”) borrowed for sound to represent 風 (“wind”), sometimes with 凡 added as a phonetic.

components.gloss: a bowl of rice on a stand

食.text: In the modern form, the bowl of rice has corrupted into the similar but unrelated 良 or 艮. The variant form 𠊊 preserves the original composition.

飲.text: In the oracle bone script, it was an ideogrammic compound (會意): 酉 (“bottle (of alcoholic beverages)”) + 人 (“person”) + 口 (“mouth (occasionally with the tongue protruding)”) – a person bending over a bottle to drink the alcoholic beverage. The droplets represented drops of the drink or saliva.

首.text: Simplified from 𩠐. Originally pictogram (象形) of the head of an animal with a long mouth and horns.

香.text: In the oracle bone script, it was ideogrammic compound (會意): 黍 (“glutinous millet”) + 口 (“mouth”). The whole character perhaps indicate that millet was used to produce liquor from fermentation which could be drank and/or sacrificed.

馬.text: A horse with its head facing the left, showing a flowing mane in the wind, standing vertically on two legs. In the bronze inscriptions, the head was often simplified into an eye (目).

骨.text: 冎 is the original pictogram for this character; 肉 was added later to distinguish.

髟.text: A person with long hair. Shuowen mistakes it for a compound.

魚.text: A fish. A conservative variant is 𤋳.

鳥.text: A bird with a dangling tail.

鹿.text: A deer. Current form is highly abstracted – legs have transformed to 比 – note grouping of front and rear legs, which are bent – head has transformed to middle component (similar to 凸/曲), while antlers on top and extended lip/mouth on left transformed into 广.

components.gloss: footprint pointing down; to walk slowly

麦.text: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): phonetic 來 + semantic 夊 (“footprint pointing down; to walk slowly”); according to Xu Shen, its meaning is "wheat". 來 was the original character for “wheat”.

黄.text: In the oracle bone script, 黃 was written in two forms. One depicts a person 大 with a swollen abdomen, the more detailed forms adding a dot for the navel, representing an infirm person; it is read as 尪.

黒.text: Oracle bone form uncertain, perhaps the element in 𦰩 / 堇 without 口. Bronze inscriptions added dots to a prominent head, usually read as facial tattoos 墨刑.

akubi.text: A kneeling person with mouth open for various reasons (e.g., begging 欠, speaking and/or spitting while speaking 次, blowing 吹, singing 歌, desiring 欲, being tired 軟, vomiting 歐...).

nikuzuki.text: Ribs of an animal’s torso or simply a physical representation of a slice of meat. Stylized into 月 when next to a phonetic component and 𱼀 and/or 夕 inside some characters.

ouhen.text: The character's shape was historically very similar to 王; a dot was introduced to differentiate the two.
